newsitem.title: DUBAI: Kurdish PUK says no plans to advance on Arbil.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish PUK says no plans to advance on Arbil.

text.p: Kurdish fighters of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) do not plan to advance on Arbil in northern Iraq after they retook their stronghold of Sulaimaniya, PUK leader Jalal Talabani was on Monday quoted as saying.

"We don't have a plan now to do that, because the city is surrounded by Iraqi tanks," Talabani said in an interview with the London-based al-Hayat newspaper in response to a question on whether the PUK would retake the main regional city of Arbil.
"We leave Arbil to its people," he said. Talabani said the Iraqi army "intervened today (Sunday) by launching artillery shelling on Chamchamal, then it stopped."
U.N. sources in Baghdad said PUK forces had also regained control of Chamchamal to the south of Sulaimaniya and Darbandikhan to the east.

Talabani reiterated PUK denials that Iran was involved in the recapture of Sulaimaniya, saying: "We urge the allied forces to intervene to confront any attack on the people of Kurdistan, let them confront any Iranian force if found in the region and any Iraqi force."
He said 10,000 of his fighters were in control of Sulaimaniya by Saturday night. He said his fighters counted 364 KDP bodies but only a "small number" of PUK men were killed.
